question_text: The angle of a prism is $A$ and one of its refracting surfaces is silvered. Light rays falling at an angle of incidence $2A$ on the first surface return through the same path after suffering reflection at the second (silvered) surface. The refractive index of the material is
solution: The ray retraces its path, so it strikes the second surface normally: $r_2 = 0^{\circ}$, giving $r_1 = A$. By Snell's law at the first surface, $\sin(2A) = \mu \sin A \implies 2\sin A \cos A = \mu \sin A \implies \mu = 2\cos A$.

question_text: An object $O$ is placed on one side of two glass slabs $A$ and $B$ of thickness $1.5\text{ cm}$ and refractive index $1.5$ as shown. Separation between the slabs is $1.5\text{ cm}$. The position of the image of $O$, when viewed from the other side of slab $B$, will be
diagram_description: Two identical parallel glass slabs A and B, each of thickness 1.5 cm and refractive index 1.5, separated by 1.5 cm. An object O is placed 2 cm to the left of slab A, and an observer views it from the right side of slab B.
solution: The total normal shift due to both slabs is $\Delta s = 2 \times t\left(1 - \frac{1}{\mu}\right) = 2 \times 1.5\left(1 - \frac{1}{1.5}\right) = 1\text{ cm}$ toward the slabs.

question_text: Focal length of an equiconvex glass lens in air is $20\text{ cm}$. Relative refractive index of glass with respect to water is $\frac{9}{8}$. If the lens is dipped in water, then its new focal length in water is
solution: Using Lens Maker's formula, $\frac{1}{f_a} = (\mu_g - 1)\frac{2}{R} = \frac{1}{20}$ (for $\mu_g = 1.5$, $R = 20\text{ cm}$). In water, $\frac{1}{f_w} = (\mu_{g/w} - 1)\frac{2}{R} = \left(\frac{9}{8} - 1\right)\frac{2}{20} = \frac{1}{80}\text{ cm}^{-1} \implies f_w = 80\text{ cm}$.

options: Intermediate image in compound microscope is real, erect and magnified
Intermediate image in compound microscope is real, inverted, but diminished
Intermediate image in compound microscope is virtual, erect and magnified
Intermediate image in compound microscope is real, inverted and magnified
solution: In a compound microscope, the objective lens forms a real, inverted, and magnified intermediate image, which then acts as the object for the eyepiece.

question_text: An astronomical telescope has objective and ocular of focal length $100\text{ cm}$ and $1\text{ cm}$ respectively. Minimum magnifying power of the telescope is
solution: Minimum magnifying power corresponds to the normal adjustment (final image at infinity): $m_{\min} = \frac{f_o}{f_e} = \frac{100}{1} = 100$.

question_text: A convex mirror of focal length $f$ forms an image, which is $\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)$ times the size of the object. The distance of the object from the mirror is
solution: For a convex mirror, magnification $m = +\frac{1}{n} = \frac{f}{f - u}$. Solving for $u$ gives $f - u = nf \implies -u = (n - 1)f$, so the object distance is $(n - 1)f$.
